key_insight: Eliminating non-contributing ADAPT-VQE operators and using correlated one-body downfolding can make variational quantum chemistry both cheaper and more accurate within a fixed active space.
engineering_relevance: The method reduces circuit depth and optimization overhead, making ADAPT-VQE more practical for near-term quantum hardware and larger chemistry problems.
method: Detect and remove plateaued/redundant operators during ADAPT-VQE optimization.
Optionally restore the operator pool after elimination; the restoration variant converges more smoothly.
Replace the active-space Hamiltonian with an OBDF effective Hamiltonian to include dynamical correlation from outside the active space.
evidence_signal: Benchmarks on linear H6 chain, H6 lattice, H6 ring, and N2 using OpenFermion show lower iteration counts and circuit depth, with OBDF-ADAPT-VQE energies closer to FCI than standard ADAPT-VQE.
watch_item: Performance depends on reliable detection of true plateaus versus temporary slowdowns, and the approach was validated only in simulator-based benchmark systems.
paper_title: Reducing quantum resources for ADAPT-VQE via plateau-operator elimination and correlated mean-field downfolding
